new_quiz.q: What does a Timeline node do in a Blueprint?
choices: It waits a fixed time and then fires once
It changes a value smoothly over time
It records the game to a video file
It lists the events of the level in order
new_quiz.explain: A Timeline plays a curve and gives out its value on every frame. That smooth value is what moves the platform.

new_quiz.q: Why do you turn on Instance Editable for PointA and PointB?
choices: So the platform can move while the game is paused
So the variables are saved in the Timeline
So the player can change them during the game
So you can set them on each copy in the level
new_quiz.explain: Instance Editable shows a variable in the Details panel of each placed copy. Every platform in the level can then have its own two points.

new_quiz.q: The float track of the Timeline goes from 0 to 1 and back to 0. Why does it go back to 0?
choices: So the platform returns to PointA before the loop starts again
So the platform stops at PointB
So the Timeline can be compiled
So the platform moves twice as fast
new_quiz.explain: The track value is the Alpha between the two points. Going back to 0 brings the platform back to PointA, so the loop repeats without a jump.

new_quiz.q: Your platform moves from PointA to PointB and back once, and then stops. What did you forget?
choices: To add a Static Mesh
To connect BeginPlay to Play
To turn on Loop in the Timeline
To make PointB a Vector
new_quiz.explain: Without Loop the Timeline plays one time and ends. With Loop on, it starts again each time it reaches the end, so the platform never stops.

new_quiz.q: Which output pin of the Timeline runs the movement on every frame while it plays?
choices: Finished
Update
Play
Stop
new_quiz.explain: Update fires on every frame while the Timeline plays. Finished fires only once at the end, and Play and Stop are inputs.

new_quiz.q: The Lerp (Vector) node goes from PointA to PointB. What does it return when Alpha is 0.5?
choices: PointA
PointB
The sum of PointA and PointB
The point halfway between PointA and PointB
new_quiz.explain: Lerp blends between two values. Alpha 0 gives PointA, Alpha 1 gives PointB, and 0.5 gives the point in the middle.

new_quiz.q: Where do you connect the result of the Lerp (Vector) node?
choices: To Set Relative Location on the mesh
To the Play pin of the Timeline
To the PointA variable
To Event BeginPlay
new_quiz.explain: Set Relative Location moves the mesh to the blended position. Because it runs on every Update, the floor piece travels smoothly.

new_quiz.q: What do you check when you ride the platform in Play in Editor?
choices: That the platform is hidden in the game
That the Timeline has two float tracks
That you do not slide off the platform
That the platform falls when you step on it
new_quiz.explain: A moving platform only works if the player travels with it. The test is to stand on it and see that the character stays on.

new_quiz.q: What is a Pain Causing Volume?
choices: A volume that plays a sound when you enter it
A volume that blocks the player like a wall
A ready-made volume that damages anything inside it
A volume that changes the lighting inside it
new_quiz.explain: A Pain Causing Volume is the quick way to make a trap. Any actor inside it receives damage over time.

new_quiz.q: Where do you find the Pain Causing Volume?
choices: In the Place Actors panel, under Volumes
In the Content Browser, under Add
In the World Settings, under Kill Z
In the Details panel of the character
new_quiz.explain: The volume is in the Volumes group of the Place Actors panel. You drag it into the level and scale it over the trap.

new_quiz.q: Which property of the Pain Causing Volume sets how much it hurts?
choices: Mobility
Intensity
Falloff Distance
Damage Per Sec
new_quiz.explain: Damage Per Sec in the Details panel is the amount of damage the volume deals each second.

new_quiz.q: What does the Apply Damage node do?
choices: It removes an actor from the level
It sends damage to an actor
It lowers the health variable of every actor
It plays a hit animation
new_quiz.explain: Apply Damage sends an amount of damage to one actor. That actor then decides what to do with it, for example lower its health.

new_quiz.q: In the Blueprint version of the trap, which actor do you send the damage to?
choices: The Other Actor of the overlap event
The trap Blueprint itself
The Box Collision component
The first actor in the Outliner
new_quiz.explain: The overlap event of the Box Collision gives you Other Actor, which is the actor that entered the box. You call Apply Damage on it.

new_quiz.q: Your character stands in the trap but loses no health. What do you check first?
choices: That the trap has a visible mesh
That the level has a Directional Light
That the character Blueprint handles Event AnyDamage
That the trap is named BP_Trap
new_quiz.explain: Damage is only a message. The character loses health only if its Blueprint reacts to it in Event AnyDamage.

new_quiz.q: What makes a trap fair?
choices: It deals very little damage
It can be seen before it hurts
It is hidden until the player steps on it
It is placed far from the route
new_quiz.explain: A fair trap gives the player a chance to notice it and react. If it hurts without any warning, the player feels cheated.

new_quiz.q: Which of these is a good warning for a fire trap?
choices: A sound that plays after the player is hurt
A text that appears after the player dies
A trap that is the same colour as the floor
Flames and scorch marks the player sees while walking toward it
new_quiz.explain: A warning must come before the damage. Something the player can see on the way to the trap lets them choose to avoid it.

new_quiz.q: What is a checkpoint in a level?
choices: A place that ends the level
A place where the player gets more health
A place where the game is paused
A place the game remembers, so the player returns there after a fall
new_quiz.explain: A checkpoint saves progress inside a level. After dying or falling, the player continues from there and not from the start.

new_quiz.q: What does it mean to respawn?
choices: To appear again in the level
To leave the level for the main menu
To load a different level
To save the game to a file
new_quiz.explain: To respawn is to appear again in the level. In this quest the player appears again at the last checkpoint.

new_quiz.q: What does the RespawnTransform variable on the character store?
choices: The health of the character
The location and rotation where the player will appear again
The number of checkpoints in the level
The speed of the character
new_quiz.explain: A transform holds a location and a rotation. The checkpoint writes its own transform into this variable when the player touches it.

new_quiz.q: What is Kill Z?
choices: A Blueprint node that restarts the level
A volume that you drag from the Place Actors panel
The height in the World Settings below which actors are destroyed
A key that removes the selected actor
new_quiz.explain: Kill Z is a height value in the World Settings. Any actor that falls below it is destroyed.

new_quiz.q: Why can you not use Kill Z alone to send the player back to a checkpoint?
choices: It removes the character and does not bring it back
It only works on static meshes
It only works in the editor, not in the game
It moves the character to the start of the level
new_quiz.explain: Kill Z destroys the character. To move the player back, you need your own logic that runs before the character reaches that height.

new_quiz.q: Where do you place the large Box Collision of BP_KillZone?
choices: Around the checkpoint
Above the level, in the sky
Below the Kill Z height
Under the level, above the Kill Z height
new_quiz.explain: A falling player must touch your kill zone before reaching Kill Z. So the box sits under the level but above that height.

new_quiz.q: Which node moves the player back to the last checkpoint?
choices: Destroy Actor
Set Actor Transform with RespawnTransform
Apply Damage
Add to Viewport
new_quiz.explain: Set Actor Transform places the character at the stored transform. Because the checkpoint saved it, the player lands at the last checkpoint.

new_quiz.q: You touch a checkpoint, fall, and appear at the wrong place. What do you check first?
choices: That the level has a Sky Light
That the kill zone has a visible mesh
That the checkpoint stores its transform in RespawnTransform on overlap
That Kill Z is set to 0 in the World Settings
new_quiz.explain: The kill zone only moves the player to whatever RespawnTransform holds. If the checkpoint never wrote its transform into the variable, the old value is used.

new_quiz.q: What is a HUD prompt?
choices: A sound that plays when the player is near an object
A short text on the screen that tells the player what they can do
A menu that pauses the game
A light that marks an object in the level
new_quiz.explain: A HUD prompt is a short on-screen text such as Press E to open. It tells the player that an action is possible right now.

new_quiz.q: As which kind of asset do you build screen elements in Unreal Engine?
choices: Level Instances
Material Instances
Widget Blueprints
Data Assets
new_quiz.explain: Screen elements are built as Widget Blueprints. Their names often start with WBP_, as in WBP_Prompt.

new_quiz.q: How do you create a new Widget Blueprint in the Content Browser?
choices: Click Add, then User Interface, then Widget Blueprint
Click Add, then Blueprint Class, then Actor
Click Add, then Material
Click Add, then Level
new_quiz.explain: Widget Blueprints are in the User Interface group of the Add menu. You then choose User Widget as the parent.

new_quiz.q: Inside the Widget Blueprint, where do you take the Text widget from?
choices: From the Outliner
From the Place Actors panel
From the Details panel
From the Palette
new_quiz.explain: The Palette lists the widgets you can use. You drag a Text widget from it into the designer and type your line.

new_quiz.q: Which two nodes show the prompt on the screen when the player comes near?
choices: Create Widget, then Add to Viewport
Spawn Actor from Class, then Play
Remove from Parent, then Create Widget
Print String, then Add to Viewport
new_quiz.explain: Create Widget makes a widget from the class WBP_Prompt. Add to Viewport then puts that widget on the screen.

new_quiz.q: Which node hides the prompt when the player walks away?
choices: Destroy Actor
Remove from Parent
Add to Viewport
Set Actor Transform
new_quiz.explain: Remove from Parent takes the widget off the screen. You call it on End Overlap.

new_quiz.q: Why do you store the result of Create Widget in a variable?
choices: So the text can be translated
So the widget is saved to disk
So the widget is created on every frame
So you can remove the same widget later on End Overlap
new_quiz.explain: End Overlap needs to know which widget to remove. The variable keeps a reference to the widget that Begin Overlap created.

new_quiz.q: Why is the Box Collision of BP_Interactable larger than the cube?
choices: So the cube can be pushed by the player
So the cube is easier to see
So the prompt shows while the player is near the cube
So the cube blocks the camera
new_quiz.explain: The overlap must start before the player touches the cube. A larger box gives a zone around the object where the prompt is shown.

new_quiz.q: What is a pressure plate?
choices: A switch on the floor that is active only while something stands on it
A switch on the wall that stays on after one press
A floor piece that moves between two points
A volume that damages anything inside it
new_quiz.explain: A pressure plate works only while it is pressed. When the object leaves, the plate turns off again.

new_quiz.q: What does the Open event of BP_Gate do?
choices: It destroys the gate actor
It moves the gate to another level
It hides the mesh and turns off its collision
It plays a sound at the gate
new_quiz.explain: With the mesh hidden and its collision off, the player can walk through. Close shows the mesh and turns the collision on again.

new_quiz.q: How does a placed pressure plate know which gate to open?
choices: It always opens the nearest gate
It opens every gate in the level
It reads the name of the gate from the Outliner
You pick the gate in its Instance Editable variable named Gate
new_quiz.explain: The variable Gate is of type BP_Gate and is Instance Editable. In the Details panel of the placed plate you pick the gate with the eyedropper.

new_quiz.q: The plate calls Open on Begin Overlap and Close on End Overlap. What happens when the cube is pushed off the plate?
choices: The gate stays open
The gate closes
The cube is destroyed
The plate is hidden
new_quiz.explain: Leaving the Box Collision fires End Overlap, which calls Close. The gate is open only while something sits on the plate.

new_quiz.q: Which settings make the cube a physics cube that the player can push?
choices: Mobility set to Static and Cast Shadow turned on
Mobility set to Stationary and Hidden in Game turned on
Mobility set to Movable and Simulate Physics turned on
Mobility set to Static and Simulate Physics turned off
new_quiz.explain: Only a Movable mesh can simulate physics. With Simulate Physics on, the cube reacts when the character pushes it.

new_quiz.q: The cube sits on the plate, but the gate does not open. What do you check first on the cube?
choices: That Generate Overlap Events is turned on
That its material is set
That it is named Cube in the Outliner
That its scale is 1
new_quiz.explain: Without Generate Overlap Events the cube does not fire overlap events. The plate then does not notice the cube at all.

new_quiz.q: How can the plate react only to the cube and not to the player?
choices: Make the Box Collision of the plate smaller
Turn off the collision of the player
Place the plate far from the start of the level
Give the cube an Actor Tag and check Actor Has Tag on Other Actor
new_quiz.explain: The tag marks the cube. The plate checks Other Actor with Actor Has Tag and only calls Open when the tag is there.

new_quiz.q: If only the cube counts, what must the player do to pass the gate?
choices: Stand on the plate and wait
Push the cube onto the plate and leave it there
Jump over the plate
Touch the gate two times
new_quiz.explain: The gate is open only while the cube sits on the plate. The player solves the puzzle by moving the cube there and then walking through.

new_quiz.q: Why do you add sound to an interaction such as opening a door?
choices: It makes the door open faster
It replaces the need for a door mesh
It tells the player that their action worked, or that it did not
It stops other sounds in the level
new_quiz.explain: Sound is feedback. One sound for opening and a different sound for locked lets the player understand the result at once.

new_quiz.q: Which node plays a sound at a place in the level?
choices: Add to Viewport
Play Sound at Location
Set Relative Location
Apply Damage
new_quiz.explain: Play Sound at Location plays the sound you pick in its Sound pin at the position given in its Location pin.

new_quiz.q: What do you connect to the Location pin so that the sound comes from the door?
choices: Get Actor Location
Get Player Controller
Event BeginPlay
The IsLocked variable
new_quiz.explain: Get Actor Location returns the position of the door actor. The sound then plays from the door and not from somewhere else.

new_quiz.q: What does the Branch on IsLocked do in the door graph?
choices: It plays both sounds at the same time
It locks the door for ever
It repeats the sound until the player leaves
It chooses one of two paths, each with its own sound
new_quiz.explain: A Branch runs its True output or its False output. One output plays the locked sound and the other plays the open sound.

new_quiz.q: Why is the IsLocked variable Instance Editable?
choices: So the sound can be changed during the game
So one copy in the level can be locked and another one not
So the door is saved as a Level Instance
So the Branch node can be compiled
new_quiz.explain: Instance Editable lets you set the variable on each placed copy. You place two doors, one locked and one not, and test both sounds.

new_quiz.q: The engine sounds CompileSuccess and CompileFailed do not show in the sound list. What do you do?
choices: Restart the editor
Import them from the Epic website
Click the settings icon of the list and turn on Show Engine Content
Enable the Water plugin
new_quiz.explain: These sounds are part of the engine content, which is hidden by default. Show Engine Content makes them appear in the list.

new_quiz.q: What is another way to play a sound from the door Blueprint?
choices: Add an Audio Component and call Play on it
Add a Box Collision and call Open on it
Add a Timeline and turn on Loop
Add a Text widget and call Add to Viewport
new_quiz.explain: An Audio Component is a sound source that is part of the actor. Calling Play on it starts its sound.

new_quiz.q: Why should you also send a short video clip with sound, if you can?
choices: A clip shows the nodes more clearly
A clip is smaller than a screenshot
A clip proves that the project was saved
A screenshot has no audio
new_quiz.explain: The graph screenshot shows that both sound nodes exist, but nobody can hear a picture. A clip with sound proves that the two sounds play.
